serverIdentity.ptrHint: Set it in your server provider's panel (Hetzner, DigitalOcean, Vultr…), not in DNS: {ip} → {host}. One PTR covers every domain.
serverIdentity.systemHint: Applying a mail hostname here also sets the system hostname and /etc/hosts.

connectGuide.title: Connect Device
connectGuide.subtitle: Email client settings for {email}
connectGuide.sendHelp: Send the IMAP and SMTP settings and test outbound delivery. The mailbox password will not be included.
connectGuide.guideHelp: Use these settings in Outlook, Thunderbird, Apple Mail, Gmail, or a mobile mail app.
connectGuide.step2: Use {email} as the username for incoming and outgoing servers.
connectGuide.step3: Use the mailbox password created in dPanel and enable SMTP authentication.
connectGuide.step4: Accept only a valid TLS certificate matching {host}.

apps.title: Use in your website or app
apps.help: Copy-paste SMTP settings for this mailbox. Host and username are already filled in; only add the mailbox password.
apps.laravelNote: Add these lines to your project's .env, then clear the config cache.
apps.wordpressNote: Put the constants in wp-config.php (above "That's all, stop editing") and save the second file as a must-use plugin. No extra plugin needed.
apps.ci4Note: Add to the project's .env. Values override app/Config/Email.php.
apps.ci3Note: Create this file; the email library loads it automatically.
apps.phpmailerNote: For plain PHP sites. Install PHPMailer with Composer first.
apps.symfonyNote: The {'@'} in the username is URL-encoded as %40. URL-encode the password too if it has special characters.
apps.nodeNote: Uses Nodemailer. Keep the password in an environment variable.
apps.pythonNote: Standard library only, no packages needed.
apps.djangoNote: Add to settings.py; send_mail() then uses this mailbox.
apps.passwordHint: Replace {placeholder} with the mailbox password. Keep it in .env or server config, never commit it to Git. Port 587 with STARTTLS (tls) also works if 465 is blocked.

form.liveHelp: Real mail: delivered to any address, inside or outside this server.
form.sandboxHelp: Mail reaches mailboxes on this server only. Nothing is sent outside.

create.title: Create Email
create.subtitle: Create a new mailbox account.
create.ipHelp: Applies to the whole domain: MX and SPF must then use this IP and hostname (see Mail DNS Guide).

dnsGuide.applyConfirm: Add these records to the {zone} zone on this server? Existing MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC and mail host records are replaced.
dnsGuide.title: Mail DNS Setup Guide
dnsGuide.subtitle: Real records for Cloudflare or dPanel DNS.
dnsGuide.noDomains: No real website or mailbox domain exists yet. Create the domain first; this guide does not display demo records.
dnsGuide.hostWrong: The mail host {host} points to {resolved}, not this server ({server}). Mail sent to it goes to the wrong machine. Point its A record here (DNS only, not proxied), or set {env} in {file} to a name that does.
dnsGuide.noServerIp: Server IP is not configured. Set {env} in {file}; do not publish the A record until its real value appears here.
dnsGuide.dkimMissing: DKIM public key is not configured.
dnsGuide.dkimMissingFor: DKIM public key is not configured for {domain} (configured: {configured}).
dnsGuide.recordsHelp: Use the same values in Cloudflare DNS or dPanel DNS Zones. TTL: Auto/3600.
dnsGuide.hostedHere: This domain's DNS is hosted here ({zone} zone)
dnsGuide.ptrWhere: Set by your server provider, not in DNS
dnsGuide.hostWhere: Set in the zone of the mail host
dnsGuide.ptrPurpose: Gmail rejects mail when this does not resolve back to the server IP
dnsGuide.ptr6Purpose: Mail goes out over IPv4 only until the IPv6 address has reverse DNS
dnsGuide.hostPurpose: Mail host must point to this server
dnsGuide.host6Purpose: Optional: lets other servers reach the mail host over IPv6
dnsGuide.bimiHelp: Gmail, Yahoo and Apple Mail show this logo as the sender picture next to mail from {domain}. Upload any square image — PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF or SVG — and the panel traces it into the SVG Tiny PS file BIMI needs, hosts it, and adds the {record} record above.
dnsGuide.bimiDmarc: DMARC must enforce: with a logo the DMARC row above switches to {policy}. Make sure SPF and DKIM pass first.
dnsGuide.bimiVmc: Yahoo shows it once DMARC enforces. Gmail and Apple also need a VMC or CMC certificate from DigiCert or Entrust, added as {tag} in the BIMI record.
dnsGuide.bimiConvert: A converted image is traced into flat shapes, so small text and gradients are simplified. A logo exported as SVG Tiny PS by a designer looks best.
dnsGuide.bimiNoHttps: The panel URL is not https, so the logo cannot be published. Enable SSL for the panel domain first.

cf.step1: Open domain → DNS → Records and add every configured row above.
cf.step2: The {mail} A record must be {dnsOnly} (grey cloud), never Proxied.
cf.step3: MX target is {host}, priority 10. Never put an IP in MX.
cf.step4: Paste TXT values without adding quotes; Cloudflare handles them.

dp.step0: This domain's zone is hosted here: use {button} above to add every row in one click (existing mail records are replaced).
dp.step2: Add the same rows above with TTL 3600.
dp.step3: For MX, enter priority 10 separately and content {host}.
dp.step4: Do not create duplicate SPF records; merge allowed senders into one SPF TXT record.

after.title: After publishing
after.body: Verify MX, SPF, DKIM and DMARC after propagation. Keep DMARC at {none} while monitoring; move to {quarantine} or {reject} only after SPF and DKIM pass consistently. Ask the hosting provider to set reverse DNS/PTR for the server IP to {host}; PTR cannot be created in Cloudflare or dPanel DNS.

hostnameCard.useConfirm:
Use {host} as the mail hostname?

Every domain's MX record must then be changed to {host}; until you do, Verify DNS shows MX as wrong.
hostnameCard.setFailed: Could not set the mail hostname.
hostnameCard.title: Mail hostname
hostnameCard.help: The name this server announces when sending mail, and the MX target for every domain. It must resolve to this server. Updates pick it automatically.
hostnameCard.noAnswer: DNS did not answer; refresh to check again
hostnameCard.noCandidates: No candidates. Add an A record (DNS only) such as mail.<panel domain> pointing to this server.
hostnameCard.noneResolve: No candidate resolves to this server yet. Add an A record (DNS only, not proxied) for mail.<panel domain> pointing here, then apply.

ipsCard.removeConfirm: Remove {ip}? Its domains move to the default IP and need their MX and SPF updated.
ipsCard.title: Mail IPs & SSL
ipsCard.help: Each IP has one hostname: its HELO name, the MX of its domains, and the name its PTR must give. Each hostname gets its own certificate for SMTP (587/465) and IMAP (993). Certificates renew automatically every day.
ipsCard.generating: Generating… (up to a minute per hostname)
ipsCard.askProvider: Ask your provider to set it to {host}
ipsCard.noOther: No other public IP on this server's interfaces. Add the IP to the server first (provider panel + netplan).
ipsCard.hostnameLabel: Hostname (A record → this IP, DNS only)
ipsCard.perDomainHelp: After changing a domain's IP, update its MX and SPF from the Mail DNS Guide.

health.title: Mail Health
health.subtitle: Delivery failures, queue health, spam signals, and suggested fixes
health.pausedHelp: Mail to other servers waits in the queue and is sent automatically once the PTR is fixed, or as soon as you turn off "{option}" below. Ask your IP provider to set the PTR (reverse DNS) of the server IP to your mail hostname, and make sure that hostname's A record points back to the IP.
health.holdMail: Hold mail if PTR is wrong
health.problemsHelp: Dovecot cannot find these, so mail for them bounces. In {link}, turn the mailbox off and on again: turning it on runs every check and shows which one fails.
health.logsHelp: The panel reads the Postfix log through the execution service ({script}). Make sure drust is running and its runtime scripts are up to date, or set {env} to a log under {dir}. Queue data may still be available.
health.blockedTitle: Outside servers Postfix refused (relay attempts, unknown recipients). Your server blocking them is healthy, so they do not lower the score.
health.holdTitle: When on, outbound mail waits in the queue while the server IP's PTR is wrong, instead of bouncing at Gmail.
health.downloadTitle: Downloads the most recent 20,000 mail log lines

records.title: Mail DNS records

records.noIpv6: No public IPv6 on this server

records.domainHelp: Add these in the zone of every domain that sends or receives mail. Open the Mail DNS Guide for a domain to get its real DKIM and DMARC values, or to add them to dPanel DNS in one click.
